evidence: In every frame the pot sits on the large left burner, with the kettle standing upright right behind it at the back of the left burner grate. Blue flame is visible at the left edge of that burner throughout (left shoulder view; wrist camera at 54.4-57.6 s). So the kettle is on the stove and the left burner is lit. Neither the kettle nor the pot is held; the arm only moves around the front-left of the cooktop (52.8 s at the left knob, then lifting and turning away), with no new change to the scene. Caveat: the pot, not the kettle, occupies the centre of the lit burner, and the kettle is crowded toward the back, so whether the kettle still counts as on the burner is somewhat uncertain.
